name.en: Takeda Ventures (Takeda Center for External Innovation)

strategy.thesis: Corporate venture arm of Takeda Pharmaceutical (Tokyo) that invests in early-stage, often preclinical, biotech companies aligned with Takeda's four core R&D pillars, feeding Takeda's own pipeline and partnership/M&A funnel.

summary.en: Takeda's in-house corporate venture group, operating since 2001, backs early-stage therapeutics and platform companies in oncology, rare genetics & hematology, neuroscience, and GI/inflammation that complement Takeda's pipeline.

sources.title: Center for External Innovation | Takeda Pharmaceuticals
sources.supports: founding year, R&D pillar focus, stage
sources.quote: Takeda Ventures concentrates on therapeutic investments aligned with four R&D pillars: Oncology, Rare Genetics & Hematology, Neuroscience and Gastrointestinal and Inflammation.

verification_notes: Operating unit (Takeda Ventures, Inc.) is based in San Diego, CA as a wholly-owned subsidiary of Tokyo-headquartered Takeda Pharmaceutical Company Limited.

strategy.thesis: Wholly-owned CVC of Astellas Pharma (Tokyo) investing in early-stage biotechnology companies developing therapeutics programs and platform technologies for drug discovery and development.

summary.en: Astellas Pharma's dedicated venture-capital subsidiary, active since 2005, backing early-stage biotech developing new therapeutics and drug-discovery platform technologies, mostly in the US/Europe.

sources.title: Strengthening Program for Pharmaceutical Startup Ecosystem / List of Registered Venture Capitals
sources.publisher: AMED (Japan Agency for Medical Research and Development)
sources.quote: Astellas Venture Management LLC - Wholly-owned venture capital organization within Astellas Pharma, investing in early-stage biotechnology companies focused on therapeutics programs

verification_notes: Operating unit historically based in Brisbane, California as a wholly-owned subsidiary of Tokyo-headquartered Astellas Pharma Inc.

name.en: Eisai Corporate Venture Investment (Eisai Innovation, Inc.)

strategy.thesis: Eisai's Corporate Venture Investment (CVI) Office pursues strategic-return minority investments to reinforce Eisai's drug-discovery platform, access cutting-edge digital technologies, and acquire drug-development technology.

summary.en: Eisai's corporate venture investment arm backs biotech (small-molecule, biologics, oligonucleotide, gene-therapy) and digital-health startups, primarily supporting Eisai's neurology-focused drug pipeline, via its US affiliate Eisai Innovation, Inc.

sources.title: Corporate Venture Capital | Innovation | Eisai Co., Ltd.
sources.quote: Eisai conducts CVC activities aimed at achieving strategic returns through financial investments, investing across biotechnology and digital/ecosystem sectors, with a portfolio including startups developing small-molecule drugs, biologics, oligonucleotides, and gene therapies, plus digital health solutions.

strategy.thesis: Launched April 2025, Shionogi CVC deploys up to ¥20 billion annually into seed-to-mid-stage ventures relevant to Shionogi's growth areas toward 2030-2040, acting as a collaborative partner rather than a passive investor.

summary.en: Shionogi's newly formalized (April 2025) corporate venture capital program, budgeted at up to ¥20 billion a year, targeting seed-to-mid-stage startups in Japan, the US, Europe and Asia that fit Shionogi's future growth themes.
summary.local: 塩野義製薬が2025年4月に開始したCVC活動。年間最大200億円を投じ、日本・米国・欧州・アジアのシード〜ミドルステージのスタートアップに投資する。

sources.title: コーポレートベンチャーキャピタル（CVC） | イノベーション | SHIONOGI
sources.supports: founding year, fund size, focus, portfolio examples
sources.quote: Founding Year: April 2025. Fund Size: Maximum 20 billion yen annually. Current investments include Restore Vision (a biotech firm developing gene therapy for vision restoration) and Dioseve (a startup creating reproductive solutions using iPS cell technology).

funds.name: Ono Venture Investment Fund I, L.P.

size.raw: US$200 million (expanded from US$100 million in Dec 2023)

strategy.thesis: US-based CVC of Ono Pharmaceutical (Osaka) investing in bio-venture companies related to drug discovery, to accelerate Ono's open-innovation pipeline.

summary.en: Ono Pharmaceutical's US venture-capital subsidiary, established May 2020, investing in drug-discovery biotech startups; expanded its fund pool to US$200 million in December 2023.

sources.title: Ono Expands Investment in Ono Venture Investment Fund I, L.P. to US$200 Million
sources.quote: Ono Expands Investment in Ono Venture Investment Fund I, L.P. to US$200 Million

name.local: 小野デジタルヘルス投資合同会社

strategy.thesis: Ono Pharmaceutical's CVC dedicated to healthcare ventures outside the core ethical-pharmaceutical business, co-creating with digital-technology startups across the healthcare field.

summary.en: Corporate venture capital vehicle of Ono Pharmaceutical (launched July 2022) that invests in digital-health and broader healthcare startups outside prescription-drug R&D, regardless of stage or location.

sources.title: Notice concerning the Start of Investment Business of Ono Digital Health Investment, GK
sources.quote: Ono Pharmaceutical established Ono Digital Health Investment, GK (ODhI) as a corporate venture capital (CVC) that invests in venture companies in the healthcare field, outside the ethical pharmaceutical drug-related field.

strategy.thesis: Kyowa Kirin's corporate venture investment activity, launched in 2022, gains early access to external drug-discovery technology and information in bone/mineral, blood cancer & rare blood disease, and rare-disease areas.

summary.en: Kyowa Kirin began CVC-style investing in October 2022, with its first deal a US$5 million stake in Flagship Pioneering-founded Cellarity, to access drug-discovery technology supporting its own new-drug pipeline.
summary.local: 協和キリンは2022年10月にCVC活動を開始。第一号案件はFlagship Pioneering創業のCellarity社へ500万ドルを投資。

sources.title: 協和キリンの CVC 活動について
sources.quote: 投資額は500万ドル（約7億2000万円）であり、Cellarity社は病気のサインとなる細胞の性質を解析する創薬技術などを持っており、協和キリンは自社の新薬開発に活用する方針です。

sources.title: 協和キリン、米バイオスタートアップに投資 創薬技術を獲得

verification_notes: Distinct from parent-group's separate consumer-health-focused 'KIRIN HEALTH INNOVATION FUND' run by Kirin Holdings (non-pharma-core, out of this slice's scope).

strategy.thesis: Chugai Pharmaceutical's Boston-based CVC subsidiary, capitalized at $200 million, targets drug-discovery technologies, novel targets, and enabling digital technologies mainly in the US and Western Europe.

people.name: John Gustofson
people.background: 25+ years in venture capital investing and business development

summary.en: Chugai Pharmaceutical established this $200 million, Boston-based corporate venture fund in 2023 (investing since Q1 2024) to access cutting-edge drug-discovery targets, technologies and digital tools mainly in the US and Western Europe.

sources.title: Chugai Venture Fund Starts Investment Activities in Drug Discovery Start-Ups to Accelerate Innovation
sources.quote: Chugai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. announced that its corporate venture capital (CVC) subsidiary in the U.S.A., "Chugai Venture Fund, LLC" (CVF) finalized establishment of a $200M venture fund based in the Boston area, MA... CVF was established in July 2023, and went into full-scale operation in the Boston area, MA, U.S.A. in January 2024.

strategy.thesis: Terumo's medtech-focused CVC, launched August 2024 with a $75M five-year commitment, backs early- to growth-stage startups in cardiovascular, blood management, cell therapy, diabetes, digital health and drug-delivery devices to feed Terumo's M&A pipeline.

summary.en: Terumo established Terumo Ventures in August 2024 as a $75 million, five-year corporate venture fund targeting early- to growth-stage medtech startups in cardiovascular, chronic disease, cell therapy, diabetes, digital health and drug delivery.

sources.title: Terumo Establishes Corporate Venture Capital "Terumo Ventures"
sources.supports: founding date, fund size, focus areas
sources.quote: Terumo Corporation established "Terumo Ventures," a Corporate Venture Capital (CVC) organization... and invests US$75 million over the next five years in early-stage companies primarily in the fields of cardiovascular disease treatment, chronic disease treatment, and digital technologies.

verification_notes: Terumo Ventures is organized as a department within Terumo Americas Holding, Inc. (US); parent Terumo Corporation is headquartered in Tokyo.

current_fund.raw: $200 million total ($50M first fund + $150M second fund)

strategy.thesis: Olympus's medtech-focused CVC invests in startups improving clinical outcomes, reducing healthcare costs and enhancing patient quality of life, with emphasis on gastrointestinal, urology and respiratory devices tied to Olympus's endoscopy leadership.

summary.en: Olympus launched its medtech corporate venture fund in November 2021 with $50M, later tripling total commitment to $200M with a second fund, backing startups in GI, urology and respiratory devices and related diagnostics.

sources.title: Olympus Launches Venture Capital Fund to Strengthen Medtech Leadership
sources.supports: founding date, initial fund size, focus

sources.title: Olympus triples down on startup investing with $150m second medtech fund
sources.quote: Japanese optics technology and medical device producer Olympus hiked its corporate venture capital allocation to $200m with the launch of a $150m second medical technology-focused fund.

verification_notes: Fund is operated out of the US (with Cerity Partners Ventures as manager); parent Olympus Corporation is headquartered in Tokyo.

strategy.thesis: Corporate venture arms of Taiho Pharmaceutical (an Otsuka group oncology specialist) focused on oncology and immune-related-disease startups, sourcing external innovation for Taiho's cancer drug pipeline.

summary.en: Taiho Pharmaceutical operates two affiliated US corporate venture entities, Taiho Ventures LLC (est. 2016) and Taiho Innovations LLC, both investing in oncology and immune-related-disease biotech to support Taiho's cancer drug-discovery pipeline.

sources.title: Strengthening Program for Pharmaceutical Startup Ecosystem / List of Registered Venture Capitals
sources.publisher: AMED (Japan Agency for Medical Research and Development)
sources.quote: Taiho Innovations, LLC - Corporate venture capital arm of Taiho Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., focusing on oncology and immune-related diseases. Taiho Ventures, LLC - Strategic corporate venture capital arm of Taiho Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., with similar therapeutic focus areas.

verification_notes: Two distinct legal entities (Taiho Ventures LLC est. 2016 and Taiho Innovations LLC est. ~2019) both registered as Taiho Pharmaceutical's CVC arms per AMED; some secondary Japanese-language sources describe divergent scopes (oncology-only vs. broader domestic healthcare/consumer health) that could not be fully reconciled within budget. Merged into one entry pending clarification.

strategy.thesis: Jointly-owned venture-capital subsidiary of Mitsubishi Tanabe Pharma and Mitsubishi Chemical Holdings, investing in seed/early-stage North American and European biotech developing novel therapeutics, platform technologies, diagnostics or vaccines.

summary.en: Boston-based CVC founded in 2006, jointly owned by Mitsubishi Tanabe Pharma Corporation and Mitsubishi Chemical Holdings, investing in seed/early-stage therapeutics, platform-tech, diagnostics and vaccine companies in North America and Europe.

sources.title: MP Healthcare Venture Management - MPH is the venture capital arm of Mitsubishi Tanabe Pharma
sources.supports: parent company, founding year, HQ location, focus
sources.quote: MP Healthcare Venture Management is a venture capital arm of Mitsubishi Tanabe Pharma based in Boston, Massachusetts, founded in 2006. ... typically invests in seed and early-stage biotech companies, based primarily in North America and Europe, who are working on novel therapeutics, platform technologies, diagnostics, or vaccines.

sources.title: About Us — MP Healthcare Venture Management

verification_notes: Jointly owned by Mitsubishi Tanabe Pharma Corporation (MTPC) and Mitsubishi Chemical Holdings Corporation (MCHC); both Japan-headquartered parents.

strategy.thesis: Santen's US-based CVC fund, established 2017 with $50M capacity, leverages the company's ophthalmology-specialty expertise to co-invest alongside other VCs in platform technology, gene/cell therapy, devices/drug-delivery systems and biomarker startups in eye disease.

summary.en: Santen Pharmaceutical (Osaka), the world's largest pure-play ophthalmology company, set up a $50 million US corporate venture fund in 2017 to co-invest in early-stage ophthalmology biotech and devices, covering glaucoma, dry eye, AMD, myopia and other eye diseases.

sources.title: 参天製薬、米国でのコーポレートベンチャーキャピタルファンドの設立を決定
sources.quote: In 2017, Santen decided to establish a corporate venture capital fund (Santen Venture Capital Fund) in the US with a total investment capacity of $50 million, leveraging its deep expertise and networks as an ophthalmology specialty company.

name.local: シコニア・バイオベンチャーズ株式会社

strategy.thesis: Joint drug-discovery incubation vehicle backed by Takeda, Astellas and Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation that evaluates early-stage drug-discovery seeds originating in Japan, founds new biotech companies around them, and raises global follow-on capital.

summary.en: Ciconia Bioventures is a Takeda/Astellas/SMBC-backed joint venture (established 2024, HQ Fujisawa) that incubates early Japan-originated drug-discovery programs into newly founded biotech startups and helps them raise global capital.
summary.local: 武田薬品、アステラス製薬、三井住友銀行が共同出資して2024年に設立したシコニア・バイオベンチャーズは、日本発の創薬シーズを評価し自ら企業を設立、グローバルに資金調達を行う。

sources.title: Joint Venture Company Established for Incubation of Early Drug Discovery Programs; Investment from Takeda, Astellas and Sumitomo Mitsui Banking
sources.quote: Ciconia seamlessly covers the entire process from early drug discovery research to establishment of biotech startups, with the aim of translating innovative technologies and drug discovery programs originating in Japan into clinical applications... Ciconia will evaluate early development stage seeds, establish its own company based on the selected seeds, raise funds worldwide and pursue global product development, according to Toshio Fujimoto, the company's Representative Director and Founder CEO.

sources.title: Ciconia Bioventures—Revolutionizing Japan's Drug Discovery Ecosystem in the Quest for Global Leadership

strategy.thesis: Sysmex, the diagnostics company (blood/urine/cell testing ~99% of sales), does not run a dedicated CVC fund vehicle but makes direct balance-sheet strategic investments in startups as part of its 'open innovation' strategy, coordinated via its Sysmex Open Innovation Lab (SOLA) in Kobe and Healthcare Science Hub Tokyo.

summary.en: Sysmex, a Kobe-headquartered global leader in diagnostic testing, invests directly from its balance sheet in startups (e.g. retinal-regenerative-medicine developer VC Cell Therapy) as part of an open-innovation strategy rather than through a dedicated CVC fund.

sources.title: シスメックス株式会社 | 事業概要・投資方針・投資実績
sources.supports: investment structure (no dedicated CVC subsidiary), SOLA lab
sources.quote: Sysmex is a diagnostics company... The company does not have a dedicated CVC subsidiary, but instead invests directly from its balance sheet and positions 'open innovation' as a clear strategy... established an open innovation lab 'Sysmex Open Innovation Lab. (SOLA)' within its Techno Park R&D hub in Kobe.

sources.title: VCCT Inc. raised 600 million Japanese yen through Third-Party equity allotment
sources.supports: example investment (Sysmex participated alongside DAI-DAN and YASKAWA)

verification_notes: No dedicated CVC fund entity or disclosed capital pool found; included because Sysmex is a named anchor and demonstrably makes recurring direct strategic investments in medical startups. Confidence kept low pending a clearer institutional vehicle.

strategy.thesis: Rather than running an in-house CVC fund, Daiichi Sankyo (and predecessor Sankyo) has historically taken LP stakes in external healthcare venture funds to gain early information access on US/European life-science startups and identify in-licensing/co-development partners.

summary.en: Daiichi Sankyo (formerly Sankyo) has been an LP investor in an external 'healthcare venture fund' since 2003, renewing into a 'Second Fund' by 2006, primarily to scout US/European life-science startups for in-licensing and co-development deals, rather than operating a dedicated in-house CVC vehicle.

sources.title: DAIICHI SANKYO to Invest in the Healthcare Venture Fund
sources.supports: LP investment structure, history, preferential rights, notable sourced deal
sources.quote: Daiichi Sankyo is granted preferential rights including guarantee of status as a sole pharmaceutical partner participating in the Fund... Sankyo obtained various outcomes to assess the possibility of in-license such as CS-9803 (KAI Pharmaceuticals Inc.) and co-development through the information from the First Fund.

verification_notes: Primary evidence is a circa-2006 press release; could not verify whether this LP program or a successor is still active as of 2026, nor find a more recent dedicated Daiichi Sankyo CVC vehicle (Daiichi Sankyo Healthcare, the OTC subsidiary, separately runs a vaguer 'open innovation'/startup-collaboration program with no disclosed fund size). Status marked unknown pending fresher sourcing.
